demonstrated_gap: The layer has never run native workers against any challenger, and the GPT-family worker path has never been measured. Codex rust-v0.157.0 (2026-09-25) turns subagents on by default. It sets model and reasoning effort per agent, caps concurrency with an [agents] setting, returns snapshots from close_agent (#47252) and cleans up cancelled child agents (#47348). In non-interactive flows it passes failures that need approval back to the parent. These map directly onto the layer's cancellation and preserved-failure checks. The trial needs no new credential: it uses the native ChatGPT sign-in, and the stack already pins 0.155.1. Caveat: the docs say subagents inherit the parent's sandbox and never mention a worktree per subagent. Edit ownership therefore has to come from Worktrunk's Codex plugin or from separate processes, and the trial must measure exactly that.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Use the frozen coding/research task with fixed acceptance commands. Arm A: Codex 0.157.x subagents with custom agent files, agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session set, and default_subagent_model and default_subagent_reasoning_effort matched to the task. Arm B: a Claude Code >=2.1.283 Workflow with isolation: worktree routed through Worktrunk hooks. Score each arm on (1) independent acceptance pass; (2) stopping mid-run leaves no orphan child threads or edits; (3) each child's writes stay inside the worktree it owns, and colliding writes to a shared tree count as a fail; (4) a failed child's result reaches the parent verbatim; (5) returned usage reconciles with the provider counters. If Codex matches acceptance and passes ownership and cancellation with complete usage, it becomes a co-equal worker lane. If it fails ownership, it stays a single-worker or reviewer lane.
evidence: https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.157.0: published 2026-09-25. Lists #47235 (multi-agent spawning routed through SpawnRequest), #47240 (fix for V2 agent eviction racing queued messages), #47244 (agent resume handling centralized), #47252 (close_agent returns agent snapshots) and #47348 (subagent spawn persistence overlapped, cancelled children cleaned up).

demonstrated_gap: The layer's overturn condition names approval waits, effect recovery and replay. The winners' hard-crash and reboot behaviour is unqualified, and worker recovery covers only one synthetic task. Archon runs YAML DAGs committed to the repository. Each run gets its own git worktree. Runs mix deterministic bash validation nodes and review nodes with an interactive approval gate that pauses for input. Run state is stored in SQLite or PostgreSQL. It has ownership-aware cancellation: /workflow cancel refuses when no owner answers and records the owner's host and pid. /workflow resume re-runs a failed or paused run and skips completed nodes, and there are also approve, reject and abandon commands. Its README says it computes provider-reported token totals per run across resumed segments and flags when a total is only a floor. That bears directly on the layer's unresolved accounting gap. The Claude provider can use the native `claude /login` through CLAUDE_USE_GLOBAL_AUTH=true. Two constraints apply. Telemetry is on by default and must be disabled with ARCHON_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. The Codex provider docs tell users to copy tokens out of ~/.codex/auth.json into .env, which breaks the credential policy, so the trial is Claude-only.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Run the frozen task as an Archon DAG (Claude global auth, telemetry disabled, SQLite): plan, implement in a worktree, bash validate, review, approval gate, PR. Compare it with the native Claude Workflow on (a) kill -9 during implement, then /workflow resume skips completed nodes with no duplicated commits or external effects; (b) /workflow cancel stops the run after checking the owner and keeps the worktree with its edits; (c) an approval wait survives an orchestrator restart and completes on approve or reject; (d) run usage reconciles with Claude-reported usage; (e) independent acceptance is equal. Archon earns the approval-wait and restart role only if it passes (a) through (d) where the native Workflow fails its crash/restart case. Otherwise it falls back to keep_but_compare.
evidence: https://github.com/coleam00/Archon (README): 'Every workflow run gets its own git worktree'. Shows deterministic bash nodes and an 'interactive: true # Pauses and waits for human input' approval loop. Storage is 'SQLite / PostgreSQL (14 core tables)' and providers are Claude, Codex and Pi. Telemetry is on by default, with ARCHON_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 to opt out. The telemetry section describes provider-reported token totals per run 'across all of its resumed segments', flagged when they are a floor.

demonstrated_gap: This is the closest design match to the overturn condition's replay and ownership cases. The scheduler is deterministic with no LLM in the coordination loop. A replay journal lets `bernstein replay latest --verify` name the first step that diverged. `bernstein workflow resume` checkpoints every node and refuses to run a changed manifest digest. Each coding task gets its own worktree behind merge gates, and a janitor verifies with tests and lint. It has Claude Code and Codex CLI adapters, and `bernstein doctor` checks the native CLI authentication. It installs with `uv tool install`. It signs run receipts that can be verified offline, which fits this repository's receipt practice. It is not worth a trial now for two reasons. It declares itself a solo-maintained beta. It also published 11 repository advisories (9 high) between 2026-08-12 and 2026-09-10, and they hit exactly the properties this layer needs: worktree-isolation escape, claim-scope bypass, hooks bypassing workspace trust, and audit verify reporting success on a critical finding.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Run the trial once 60 days pass with no new high advisory, or earlier if Archon fails the replay case. Run the frozen task through `bernstein workflow`, CLI only, with the server, Slack, hosted-MCP and volunteer features off, using the Claude Code adapter, against the native Workflow. It passes if replay --verify reproduces the task graph, resume after kill -9 skips completed nodes and refuses a modified manifest, an attempted write into another worktree is blocked, the run receipt verifies offline, and acceptance and usage are equal or better.

Documents the replay journal and `bernstein replay latest --verify`, and `bernstein workflow resume <run_id>`, which resumes at the first non-completed node and validates the manifest digest. Says 'Each coding task gets its own git worktree behind merge gates'. Lists adapters for Claude Code, Codex CLI and others. Install is `uv tool install bernstein`.

demonstrated_gap: It is the only candidate that has published a head-to-head against a native baseline. On LHTB (46 tasks, GPT-5.6 Sol at max effort), LoopX 1.0.3 Heartbeat scored 0.4948 mean reward, against 0.4475 for native Codex Goal and 0.4218 for plain Codex. It keeps durable goal, gate, evidence and quota state, with peer ownership (claims and leases) and recoverable handoffs across Codex and Claude Code. That bears on the cross-session recovery gap. The limits are real. Each task and mode got one effective trial, and runtimes and budgets were unequal (the project's own caveat). Strict solves did not improve (7/46 for both LoopX and plain Codex; native Codex Goal had 4/46). Against native Goal, 23 tasks improved, 13 tied and 10 regressed. Its target is long-horizon continuation, not this layer's bounded independent tasks. It published five advisories on 2026-08-12, including OS command injection in the Visible Multi-Agent Launcher and unauthenticated path traversal in serve-status. `loopx workflow-skills --install` writes into the agent host's skills. The repository was created on 2026-05-31.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Run this when a real task spans sessions or restarts with peer handoffs. Do equal-budget runs, k>=3, of the frozen task or an LHTB subset, managed by LoopX versus native Workflow or Codex Goal, with a forced restart mid-run. LoopX wins if acceptance is higher at equal budget, ownership leases prevent cross-worker edits, evidence and handoff state survive the restart, and no new high advisory appears.
evidence: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx (README): the LHTB table shows plain Codex 0.4218, native Codex Goal 0.4475 and LoopX 1.0.3 Heartbeat 0.4948. The README itself states: 'One effective trial per task and mode; designated replacement trials and unequal runtime/budgets'. Describes 'peer ownership and recoverable handoffs' and 'peer-agent teams where ownership, leases, and handoff matter'. Install is `pip install loopx` followed by `loopx workflow-skills --install`.

demonstrated_gap: Symphony orchestrates GPT-family workers from an issue tracker. Each issue gets its own workspace and a Codex app-server session. Its tracker adapters include GitHub Issues, so it needs no new SaaS credential, and host-side auth removes tracker tokens from the Codex child. When a claimed issue reaches a terminal state, it stops the agent and cleans up the workspace, which covers cancellation. The spec recovers from restarts through tracker state without a database, and PRs carry proof of work (CI and review) before landing. That fits 'integrate only after relevant review' for a continuous issue queue. It is not ready now. Upstream calls the Elixir implementation a prototype for evaluation only and recommends building a hardened implementation of SPEC.md. Blocked approvals are held only in memory and cleared on restart, so it fails the approval-wait case. It is at v0.0.3, supports Codex only, and needs the Elixir/Erlang toolchain.
comparison_that_would_overturn: Run this if work becomes a continuous GitHub-Issues queue for Codex. Feed 3 frozen issues through the GitHub Issues adapter and compare with native Workflow plus Worktrunk: (1) closing an issue mid-run stops the agent and cleans the workspace with no stray commits; (2) after an orchestrator restart, work is re-dispatched without duplicate PRs or effects; (3) an approval-blocked issue survives the restart (expected to fail on the current prototype); (4) each PR carries CI and review proof. It overturns only when a maintained implementation persists blocked state and passes all four.
evidence: https://github.com/openai/symphony (README): 'Symphony is a low-key engineering preview for testing in trusted environments.' Option 1 is to implement SPEC.md yourself. Apache-2.0.

https://github.com/openai/symphony/blob/main/elixir/README.md: 'prototype software intended for evaluation only'. Adapters: Linear, GitHub Issues, Jira Cloud, Asana, GitLab. Creates a workspace per issue and launches Codex in App Server mode. When a claimed issue reaches a terminal state, Symphony 'stops the active agent for that issue and cleans up matching workspaces'. 'Blocked entries are in memory only; restarting the orchestrator clears that blocked map.'

https://github.com/openai/symphony/blob/main/SPEC.md: tracker-agnostic Issue Tracker Adapter; 'Poll the issue tracker on a fixed cadence and dispatch work with bounded concurrency'; 'Support tracker/filesystem-driven restart recovery without requiring a persistent database'.
